content:
Let \(L\) be the side length of the square pond.  
On day 1, the open water is the inner square of side \(L-20\), so

\[
(L-20)^2 = 0.65L^2.
\]

Taking square roots:

\[
L-20 = \sqrt{0.65}\,L
\]

\[
L(1-\sqrt{0.65})=20
\]

\[
L=\frac{20}{1-\sqrt{0.65}}.
\]

The pond is completely frozen when the inner open square vanishes:

\[
L-20n \le 0 \implies n \ge \frac{L}{20}.
\]

Thus

\[
n \ge \frac{1}{1-\sqrt{0.65}} \approx 5.16.
\]

So the smallest integer day is

\[
\boxed{6}.
\]
